title: Four games made of live elements
blurb: Draggable notes that leave the canvas with their drawn pixels as the drag image, a 16 by 16 picture whose pixels are checkboxes in a form, a same-origin <iframe> cut into a sliding puzzle whose tiles still scroll and click, and a contenteditable page with a corner that curls and shows the typed text in reverse.
question: When a canvas draws one element in several places, or leaves it out, where does input go: can a drawn card start a native drag, can nine tiles of one iframe each scroll and click, and can a page be typed on while part of it is drawn mirrored?
result: Yes for all three, with extra work each time. An element has one hit region and the element drawn last is on top, so the puzzle moves the iframe's region under the pointer and covers the rest with transparent elements, and the notebook ends each frame with a hidden draw of the page at its flat place. A drawn card started a native drag with a mouse. An emulated long press did not, so touch has a second route with pointer events.
